objective: Orchestration loop refinement addressing 3 bottlenecks: scope definition, parallelism constraints, validation overhead

bottlenecks.title: Scope Definition Bottleneck
bottlenecks.description: Ambiguity in what constitutes 'done' for fleet control actions, especially 'all' targets without expected_hosts
bottlenecks.current_impact: Actions may complete prematurely or hang indefinitely

bottlenecks.title: Parallelism Constraints
bottlenecks.description: Branch desynchronization across parallel fleet execution; missing/stale branch references break worktree pipelines
bottlenecks.current_impact: Parallel improvements fail silently when branches diverge across machines

bottlenecks.title: Validation Overhead
bottlenecks.description: Insufficient distributed validation during orchestration; no systematic test/audit coverage for fleet resilience
bottlenecks.current_impact: Build failures and fleet degradation undetected until production impact

tasks.title: Implement _control_done logic for fleet control completion detection
tasks.description: Add _control_done(target, handled_by, params) function to distinguish single-host (always done) from multi-host 'all' targets (done when expected_hosts all acked)
changes: Add _control_done function after _target_matches (line 133)
Update process_controls to call _control_done instead of hardcoded target != 'all' check (line 235)
acceptance_criteria: Single-target controls always complete after one ack
'all' target without expected_hosts never completes
'all' target with expected_hosts completes when all acks received
20+ unit tests pass covering edge cases (duplicates, order, case sensitivity)

tasks.title: Extend fleet_control.py with expected_hosts parameter support
tasks.description: Ensure expected_hosts parameter is properly threaded through control request lifecycle: creation, ack tracking, and completion
changes: Verify create_control accepts and stores expected_hosts in params
Verify get_control_status returns expected_hosts for 'all' targets
Add comprehensive test scenarios for multi-host control workflows
acceptance_criteria: expected_hosts parameter flows through control lifecycle unchanged
'all' controls with expected_hosts=['m1','m2','m3'] track partial acks correctly
Integration test: 3-machine config push waits for all 3 acks before marking done

tasks.title: Add fail-soft error handling and edge case coverage for _control_done
tasks.description: Harden _control_done against None params, missing keys, empty lists, duplicates, and type mismatches
changes: Wrap expected_hosts access with .get() and default to []
Handle None, empty, and non-list expected_hosts gracefully
Add 20+ edge-case test scenarios (empty string, whitespace target, large fleet, duplicates)
acceptance_criteria: No exceptions raised on malformed input
Edge case tests all pass (empty, None, whitespace, duplicates, case-sensitivity)
Large fleet scenario (10+ machines) handles correctly
Stats and logging capture errors for diagnostics

tasks.title: Implement branch_rerouter core: existence check and stale detection
tasks.description: Add _branch_exists, _get_commit, _is_stale functions to detect missing and stale branch references across the fleet
changes: Implement _branch_exists using git show-ref --verify for local and remote branches
Implement _get_commit using git rev-parse to fetch commit SHA
Implement _is_stale using git merge-base --is-ancestor to check if commit is in canonical history
Add timeout handling via _get_timeout_sec environment variable (default 30s)
acceptance_criteria: _branch_exists detects local and remote branches correctly
_get_commit retrieves correct SHA or None if not found
_is_stale detects branches with diverged commits
Git timeout handled gracefully (returns failure, not exception)
20+ git operation mocking tests pass with CompletedProcess simulation

tasks.title: Implement branch_rerouter rerouting strategy: explicit mapping and fallback
tasks.description: Add reroute(branch) function with config-driven explicit mappings (ORCH_BRANCH_REROUTE_*) and fallback strategy
changes: Implement _get_reroute_config to parse ORCH_BRANCH_REROUTE_* env vars
Implement _get_fallback to return ORCH_BRANCH_REROUTE_FALLBACK or 'main' default
Implement _get_enabled, _get_strategy, _get_timeout_sec config accessors
Implement reroute(branch) to check explicit mappings, stale status, and fallback
Add event emission via events.emit on reroute detection
Add thread-safe stats tracking and _load_repo repo detection
acceptance_criteria: Existing branches return unchanged
Missing branches use explicit mapping or fallback
Stale branches reroute to canonical when configured
Thread-safe concurrent reroute calls work correctly
Stats track rerouted, stale_detected, errors counters
Config keys (ENABLED, STRATEGY, TIMEOUT_SEC, FALLBACK) work as documented
30+ test cases pass covering normal, missing, stale, explicit mapping, and edge cases

tasks.title: Register and wire periodic job framework for editorial, adversarial_fleet, fleet_e2e_audit
tasks.description: Add three new periodic jobs to JOBS registry with proper module imports and locking mechanism
changes: Add run_editorial, run_adversarial_fleet, run_fleet_e2e_audit functions with lazy module imports
Register all three in JOBS dict (alongside existing spec, chaos, txn, scout, deploy, roi, stuck_reaper, priority_scorer, quarantine_gc)
Add job docstrings explaining purpose and invocation pattern
Verify _run_job_locked mechanism gates concurrent execution via fcntl-based file locking
acceptance_criteria: run_editorial imports editorial_program and calls run()
run_adversarial_fleet imports adversarial_fleet and calls run()
run_fleet_e2e_audit imports fleet_e2e_audit and calls run()
All three registered in JOBS dict and callable via JOBS[name]()
Job locks enabled by default (ORCH_PERIODIC_JOB_LOCKS=true)
Overlapping invocations skipped gracefully (BlockingIOError caught)
20+ tests pass verifying registration, invocation, and locking

Generates problem statements with root causes and impact metric
Drafts stored in database with timestamp and operator_review_status
Event emitted on completion for downstream dashboard/alerts

tasks.title: Implement adversarial_fleet and fleet_e2e_audit modules for distributed resilience testing
tasks.description: Create two parallel testing modules: adversarial_fleet for chaos injection and fleet_e2e_audit for end-to-end health verification
changes: Create adversarial_fleet.py: run() injects faults (network delays, config rollbacks, branch divergence) across all runners
Create fleet_e2e_audit.py: run() verifies fleet end-to-end health (all runners healthy, no hung tasks, branch consistency)
Both emit structured results (audit_results, adversarial_results) to database
Integrate with fleet_control 'all' target for coordinated testing across machines
Emit events: adversarial_completed, fleet_audit_completed with pass/fail status
acceptance_criteria: adversarial_fleet.run() successfully injects faults and records outcomes
fleet_e2e_audit.run() verifies fleet health across all runners
Both use fleet_control 'all' target with expected_hosts parameter to coordinate
Results stored in database for analysis (adversarial_runs, fleet_audits tables)
Events emitted on completion with pass/fail status and metrics
Automated daily/weekly scheduling via periodic.py JOBS registry
20+ integration tests pass covering coordinated multi-machine scenarios
